records.meeting_body: Central Delta-Mendota Region Management Committee (indexed as Delta-Mendota Subbasin Coordination Committee)
records.agenda_item: Item 8: Report of the representative to the Coordination Committee
records.evidence_text: One is, is when we cross the river, and talking about, talking with our neighbors about. The run of the river and the creeks, the local tributaries, and how they're managed. And then the second thing is, is… just, uh, actual, uh. Data and our representative monitoring program. Um, is it… is it good enough? I think we made strides where we're putting a few more wells in, so we think we're gonna be in good shape.
records.notes: The index files this under the Coordination Committee but the agenda and speaker show a Central Delta-Mendota GSA management committee; the 2025-10-23 CDMGSA minutes repeat that the group is working on the ISW program and RMS data collection.

records.finding: The new Stanislaus County ISW well (ISW-1-165, a replacement for RMS well 05-127) is in the monitoring network but had no water-level measurement in Q1 or Q2 2026, and staff say this is being addressed. It was the only missing water-level sample listed for the Northern region.
records.quantitative_detail: No water-level sample in Q1 and Q2 2026 at one ISW well (DMS site 06-008)
records.agenda_item: Update on PRP implementation, Q1/Q2 groundwater level data and exceedances (EKI slides)
records.evidence_text: Replacement well for 05-127, included in Annual Report in monitoring network and drilled in January 2026 ... No missing GWL or GWQ samples in Q1 and Q2 other than new ISW well in Stanislaus County that is actively being addressed.
records.notes: Packet says drilled January 2026 while the 2026-02-09 minutes give completion on 3 February 2026; the reason for the missing measurement is not stated.

records.finding: A Delta-Mendota Subbasin newsletter in the Stanislaus WAC packet lists a data-gap project funded under the subbasin's DWR SGMA implementation grant: nested monitoring wells measuring ISW and subsidence plus streamflow stations on the San Joaquin River.
records.quantitative_detail: DWR SGMA Round 1 implementation grant about $7.6 million total, 13 projects; grant extended to spring 2026
records.meeting_body: Stanislaus Water Advisory Committee (packet: Delta-Mendota Subbasin newsletter, June 2025)
records.agenda_item: Packet: Delta-Mendota Subbasin June 2025 Newsletter
records.evidence_text: This initiative provides critical monitoring improvements, including the installation of nested monitoring wells that measure interconnected surface water (ISW) and subsidence. Also included are streamflow monitoring stations along the San Joaquin River and GPS monitoring systems. ... SGMA Round 1 Implementation grant from DWR the subbasin is making great progress on the 13 high-priority projects outlined in the GSP.
records.notes: Packet newsletter, not discussed aloud; the whole grant is about 7.6 million dollars across 13 projects (extraction garbles the figure) and the monitoring project's own cost is not given.

records.finding: Stanislaus County awarded the third and last ISW monitoring well (ISW1) to the lowest bidder, below the engineer's estimate, so the grant-funded ISW network could be finished. The committee also flagged the grant's completion deadline as a watch item and expected a budget increase for construction management.
records.quantitative_detail: Low bid $124,500 for ISW1 (about $10,000+ under the engineer's estimate); previous ISW well bid about $155,000; grant: SGMA Round 1 Implementation Grant (DWR); drilling started 2026-01-12, well completed 2026-02-03
records.agenda_item: Item 14a: SGMA Round 1 Implementation Grant, ISW well construction update
records.evidence_text: Stanislaus county selected the lowest bidder Living water well drilling one with 124,500. About a little more than 10,000 less than what we anticipated from my initial estimates. ... last well they came in at about 155 and so they came under on 124.
records.notes: Grant dollar amount for the ISW wells is not stated in these passages; the 2025-10-13 meeting notes overspend on construction management and the 2025-11-10 closing action items mention the ISW completion deadline under the grant.

records.finding: To fill ISW data gaps the Delta-Mendota GSAs identified additional shallow groundwater-level and stream-gage locations in their monitoring network, according to State Water Board staff.
records.meeting_body: California State Water Resources Control Board (SGMA hearing)
records.agenda_item: Delta-Mendota Subbasin probation determination
records.evidence_text: they also established a monitoring network and monitoring frequency with additional shallow groundwater level and stream gage locations identified to fill data gaps related to interconnected surface water
records.notes: No count of new gages or wells, cost or schedule is given in this item (see the July 2025 newsletter row for the grant).

records.finding: A Northern Delta-Mendota GSA member said his district is drilling additional monitoring wells at its own expense in an area with no data, one of them another ISW monitoring well, and elsewhere in the meeting the committee raised access agreements and easements for ISW wells on private land.
records.quantitative_detail: A $400,000 monitoring-well effort (scope unclear: probably the grant well plus three district wells)
records.speaker_role: board member (unlabeled speaker for a district in the Northern DM region)
records.agenda_item: Item 8: Direction on subbasin model calibration phase approach and cost share
records.evidence_text: I'm literally in the middle of drilling monitoring wells as we speak. A 400, $400,000 effort. We just drilled the monitoring well for the, for the grant and now we're drilling three more monitoring wells for the district because we got an area that has. We have no data on. One is going to be another interconnected surface water monitoring well like we're working towards collecting that.
records.notes: Speaker and district are not identified in the transcript, and it is unclear whether $400,000 covers all four wells.

records.finding: EKI is proposing to put subsidence and ISW studies, extra monitoring wells and the modeling work into the next SGM implementation grant, saying ISW studies needed to meet DWR's BMP are a stated priority of the program. Concept proposals are expected around February 2027.
records.quantitative_detail: Concept proposals due about February 2027 per draft SGM guidelines; no dollar amount stated
records.agenda_item: Grant and project planning update (SGM implementation grant)
records.evidence_text: The SGM grant guidelines actually was released yesterday, so we are, we are going through it. ... Any studies that we need to do for subsidence ISW to comply with the bmp, those are the things that are highlighted as a priority of the sgm. So it would be very feasible to get funding for them.
records.notes: On 2026-05-04 Amir Mani also said a Prop 4 SGMA grant might fund replacement monitoring wells; 'bmp' presumably refers to DWR's ISW best management practice.

records.finding: A Northern Delta-Mendota committee member said that with the Modesto and Turlock subbasins the main concern is interconnected surface water, and that the Region needs good data from their side. A meeting with them had fallen through.
records.agenda_item: Interbasin coordination update
records.evidence_text: the most important thing with us, and that's in the Modesto Turlock sub basin is dealing sub basins is dealing with interconnected surface waters is going to be the primary concern with that because we don't really have any other major things and I, you know, just, just making sure we're getting good data from their side as well.
records.notes: Transcript is garbled and the speaker is unlabeled; the 2026-01-12 Coordination Committee facilitator also says Modesto and Turlock have specific ISW topics they want to discuss.

records.finding: State Water Board staff recommended that the Delta-Mendota GSAs revise their ISW sustainable management criteria in line with DWR's forthcoming guidance, making state guidance the stated next step for ISW.
records.meeting_body: California State Water Resources Control Board (SGMA hearing)
records.agenda_item: Delta-Mendota Subbasin probation determination
records.evidence_text: Finally, the GSAs should revise sustainable management criteria for depletions of interconnected surface water in accordance with the forthcoming guidance from DWR.
records.notes: Recommendation is for future GSP updates; the Board returned the subbasin to DWR the same day.

records.finding: Consultants and a board chair told the Subbasin GSAs that DWR has not mandated a model but its annual-report comments and ISW guidance point toward one, and DWR is expected to want a calibrated model for ISW and subsidence. The GSAs are also waiting for DWR's ISW best management practice before scheduling neighbour meetings.
records.speaker_role: mixed — consultants and board members (speakers unlabeled)
records.agenda_item: Model calibration cost share; facilitation support outreach update
records.evidence_text: So there is no specific wording that DWR says you need to develop model, but all the comments on the annual reports, their guidance on isw, their guidance and subsidence and now that they started commenting on annual reports, they might show frequently points to model indirectly without mentioning you need to specifically develop a model. ... Their expectations is that for anything subsidence related and, and likely interconnected surface water, you will have a model that is calibrated ... We are still waiting for the release of interconnected surface water BMP and we'll try to schedule Modesto and Trac around that.
records.notes: Speakers are not labeled in the transcript; the excerpts are probably an EKI consultant, the chair, and the facilitator (Lisa Beutler).

records.finding: In an interbasin meeting with Kings, both sides named interconnected surface water as a focus, and the river boundary as limiting SGMA actions. They agreed to start formal collaboration on ISW and to follow EDF's planned river study, and further meetings were tied to DWR's pending ISW guidance.
records.quantitative_detail: Interbasin meeting held 2026-06-19; two further meetings planned after DWR's ISW BMP is released
records.speaker_role: consultant — Lisa Beutler (Stantec), facilitator, summarizing the meeting
records.agenda_item: Facilitation support services: interbasin coordination update
records.evidence_text: Then we kind of focused in on the interconnected surface waters and they talked a little bit about what was most important to them. Including the reach window is a critical focus area. ... Some frustration around the money spent on modeling, but the fact that there had not been a lot of solutions really went into some discussion about the boundary along the river and how it's making the application of the SGMA actions challenging just because there isn't a lot of flexibility there. ... They wanted to do that particularly on the interconnected surface water. ... They agreed to keep Jarrett in the loop on the EDF study.
records.notes: The Kings views are second-hand through the facilitator, and 'reach window' is likely garbled; the same transcript reports a rumoured EDF study of the river and river seepage, details of which the board did not know.

records.finding: The model that produces the Subbasin's depletion estimates is not calibrated, and EKI says the Delta-Mendota and Kings subbasins are the only ones in the area without a calibrated model. EKI said calibration changes how reliable the depletion, pumping and subsidence outputs are; the ad hoc committee split roughly evenly on calibrating now or in 2027.
records.quantitative_detail: Ad hoc committee informally about half for calibrating in 2026, about half for delaying one year to 2027
records.agenda_item: Tech ad hoc report: subbasin model calibration
records.evidence_text: Basically the Delta, Mendota and Kings are basically not only two that don't have a calibrated model to be used for the calibration. ... So it's not just one section or one estimation of annual storage change. Pumping estimates come from it, depletion comes from it, subsidence comes from it. So it really changes the reliability of annual report for the next year.
records.notes: 'Depletion' in the second excerpt is not explicitly ISW depletion, though the same speaker earlier ties the model to the ISW depletion SMC; first sentence is garbled ('not only two' presumably means 'only two').

records.finding: The Delta-Mendota coordination agreement's adaptive-management exhibit sets a procedure for minimum-threshold exceedances, including those caused by a neighboring subbasin, such as depletion of interconnected surface waters. The consultant investigates, costs are shared equally by seven committee members, and the committee seeks inter-basin coordination.
records.quantitative_detail: Cost of initial investigation shared equally by the 7 Coordination Committee members (1/7 each)
records.speaker_role: GSA staff (agreement text in packet of Madera County GSA, a party to the agreement)
records.agenda_item: Packet attachment: Delta-Mendota Subbasin Coordination Agreement, Exhibit C (Adaptive Management Framework)
records.evidence_text: If there is a determination that any MT exceedance was caused by a neighboring subbasin, this should be brought back to the Coordination Committee for further discussion and potential Subbasin-wide action. Costs for initial investigation by the Subbasin-wide GSP Consultant of a MT downward trend or exceedance across Subbasin boundary lines (such as water quality issues, subsidence, or depletion of interconnected surface waters) shall be shared amongst the Coordination Committee equally between Coordination Committee members (i.e. 1/7 th each).
records.notes: Agreement text from a packet attachment (earlier drafts were dated 2025); it was not discussed at this meeting, and the final adopted version was not checked.

records.finding: Outside commenters (notably the California Sportfishing Protection Alliance) told DWR the 2024 GSP's ISW thresholds and monitoring coverage are inadequate. The board gave no formal action: it asked EKI for a cost and format for reviewing the letters, wants to hear from DWR first, and called the work preparation, not a plan change.
records.quantitative_detail: EKI Task 4 budget of about $77,000 could be repurposed; CSPA letter 113 pages; four distinct comment letters (six filed) in the 75-day public comment period
records.speaker_role: mixed — EKI consultant summarising commenters; board members
records.agenda_item: Item 8: Direction on GSP public review comment letters
records.evidence_text: the CSPA Common ladder mainly focused on interconnected surface water and also have questions about the GSP's SMC protection and also the monitoring coverage. ... I don't think it's an exercise in fixing anything or adopting a new plan, but just being prepared. ... I would like to hear a little bit from DWR first before we got too far down one. One path or another.
records.notes: The ISW criticism is the commenters', not the GSAs'; CSPA's concern (no adequate protection from depletion of interconnected surface waters) is stated in the 2026-09-02 NDM packet, and CDFW's letter also raised GDEs and ISW.

records.finding: The Northern program manager said MLRP grants are usually pursued as block grants by larger groups and that, given the timeline, a SGMA grant made more sense; EKI agreed to prioritise the SGMA grant and deferred on MLRP until guidelines appear.
records.agenda_item: Grant opportunities and project list
records.evidence_text: I know the Department of Conservation Multi Benefit Land Repurposing program. That application is supposed to be released actually in August of this month. ... Again, just my gut says that the mlrp, unless people are just, I mean those are usually done in block grants and bigger groups ... I think we definitely need to prioritize the Sigma grant on the basin GSA levels
records.notes: Speaker is labelled Hallmark Group (program manager for the Northern region); the prioritising reply is Amir Mani of EKI. Timing statements differ: on 2026-09-21 EKI said the MLRP guideline was out, while on 2026-10-07 EKI said MLRP guidelines were due by end of October.

records.finding: EKI told the Northern Delta-Mendota committee that MLRP has been very competitive, benefits from a coalition including NGOs and environmental groups and from a subbasin-level application, but ranked it lower priority for the northern group. No grantee or partner structure exists yet.
records.quantitative_detail: $200 million MLRP pot (Prop 4) per EKI
records.agenda_item: Grant opportunities (Prop 4 SGMA, MLRP, Watershed Resilience)
records.evidence_text: This one has historically been very competitive. They have increased the pot of money to $200 million. It's also being funded through Prop 4. ... They're really benefit if you have a large coalition of entities. So not just, you know, GSAs but you know, NGOs and environmental organizations and so forth, stakeholder groups to do this land repurposing. ... It's probably less of a priority for this basin, particularly for northern, but certainly something that you know, would benefit from being an application at the, at the sub basin level.
records.notes: Speaker is Anona Dutton of EKI. On 2026-10-07 EKI said the focus is first the SGM grant and then MLRP, with MLRP guidelines expected by the end of October.

records.finding: The Delta-Mendota consultant told the JPA board that the second round of the Department of Conservation MLRP is a $200 million Prop 4 allocation, likely in two rounds, split between basins funded earlier and new MLRP basins. It is a single three-to-five-year application open to GSAs, the JPA and public agencies.
records.quantitative_detail: $200 million statewide MLRP round 2 (Prop 4); grant term 3 to 5 years
records.agenda_item: Grant opportunities for the subbasin (Prop 4 SGMA, MLRP, Watershed Resilience)
records.evidence_text: This is the second round coming again from the Prop 4 bucket of funding, $200 million. This is our understanding is this is going to be probably in two rounds given. So in the first allocation of funding, it might be the case that they don't spend the entire $200 million. Part of this is for the basins that already applied last time and were funded for mlrp, and part of it is also allocated for new MLRP basins. ... The grant term is three to five years. This is different because it's Department of Conservation. So it's a single application to apply.
records.notes: Speaker is Amir Mani of EKI, the subbasin technical consultant (named in other transcripts); no Delta-Mendota grantee exists yet. The same item recommends a subbasin-wide application.

records.section: 2.5 Data Source and ET Product Choice
records.finding: A San Luis Water District representative cautioned the JPA that aerial imagery or Land IQ land-use inputs to the subbasin model do not represent districts like his, which he said are more than half fallow (the transcript renders fallowed as valid).
records.quantitative_detail: San Luis Water District more than 50% fallowed (speaker's statement, no basis year)
records.agenda_item: Public comment during consideration of model calibration phase approach
records.evidence_text: I just want to be very cautious of the land use assumptions in the modeling. Using some type of aerial imagery or land IQ doesn't really represent districts like San Luis Water District that are over 50% valid.
records.notes: Minutes in the 2026-06-08 coordination committee packet record this as Lon Martin (San Luis Water District) citing aerial imagery and LandIQ and a district over 50% fallowed. The transcript word valid is a mis-transcription of fallowed. This is a land-use input to groundwater modelling, not a savings calculation. The reply from another speaker about native grasses on fallow fields is too garbled to quote.

records.finding: EKI listed the state MLRP's eligible project categories for the Delta-Mendota JPA board: groundwater recharge and floodplain restoration, agricultural land transition (repurposing, recropping), habitat restoration and water quality improvements, and community resilience, noting such projects are under way in other MLRP basins.
records.agenda_item: Grant opportunities for the subbasin (Prop 4 SGMA, MLRP, Watershed Resilience)
records.evidence_text: groundwater recharge and floodplain restoration in terms of supply augmentation, agricultural land transition in terms of repurposing the land recropping, habitat restoration and water quality improvements, and community resilience and regional implementation strategies.
records.notes: Speaker is Amir Mani of EKI describing the state programme, not a local project. No co-benefit quantification method is mentioned.

records.finding: SLDMWA staff said the San Joaquin Valley Water Collaborative Action Plan is developing a prioritization tool intended to evaluate and rank water and land repurposing projects. No criteria, co-benefit metrics or schedule were given.
records.meeting_body: San Luis & Delta-Mendota Water Authority Board
records.agenda_item: Water policy and resources update (Collaborative Action Plan)
records.evidence_text: Should be used to aid in evaluating and ranking ... and land repurposing projects.
records.notes: Speaker is Brandon Souza (SLDMWA staff). The transcript interleaves speaker labels mid-sentence, so the two excerpts are the exact fragments. The tool is valley-wide, funded by Reclamation, and assigned here to Delta-Mendota by default; the 2026-03-05 board report says the CAP is wrapping up its project prioritization tool.

records.finding: A committee member from the Northern region said they have no land repurposing projects and want MLRP money to start an incentive programme for out-of-district landowners, because land repurposing is how they expect to meet demand reduction targets. They asked the subbasin to partner on a package.
records.agenda_item: Grant opportunities and project list
records.evidence_text: I am very interested in securing some money to help start a program for out of district landowners because we don't have any projects and in order to meet our demand reduction targets, we're going to have to provide some incentives to help them ... We're going to need support and land repurposing because that's the way that we're going to be able to achieve our sustainability goals and meet our demand reduction targets.
records.notes: Speaker is labelled City of Patterson in the transcript but refers to doing it at the county GSA level, so the represented agency is uncertain. No programme design or accounting method was discussed.

records.finding: In the Northern region committee, one member said he had pushed for bare-minimum outreach on the well mitigation policy because the public had already had plenty of chances to hear about it. This is a procedural-equity stance on notice and access, not a GSA decision.
records.agenda_item: Item: communications subcommittee report
records.evidence_text: I pushed for just doing the bare minimum. ... I just feel like going above and beyond is… kind of a waste of time and energy for this group? ... the public has had plenty of opportunities to learn about this.
records.notes: Speaker unlabelled (committee member inferred); personal view, later committee direction went further (see 2025-10-13 and 2025-11-05 rows). Dimension: procedural.

records.finding: An Aliso Water District board speaker said the State Board's hold-ups were about water quality mitigation responsibilities toward underserved, disadvantaged communities with domestic wells, and that the subbasin had gone as far as the Board asked. The public record shows no GSA reply to the underlying equity concern.
records.agenda_item: Item: SGMA / probation update
records.evidence_text: most of the issues we were hung up on were around water quality mitigation responsibilities to kind of underserved communities disadvantage yeah domestic wells I think we've made the strides that they were requesting to get there
records.notes: Speaker unlabelled; role (manager or director) and the exact State Board action are unclear from the transcript. Dimension: distributive.

records.finding: A staff memo sets out DWR's template for outreach to disadvantaged communities, which includes direct outreach to drinking-water well users, accessible times and places, the users' preferred language and plain-language materials. It proposes a webinar inviting Self-Help Enterprises and Community Water Center.
records.agenda_item: Item 9: direction on domestic well mitigation policy outreach
records.evidence_text: The DWR Well Mitigation Template outlines expectations for outreach to disadvantaged communities. These include guidelines for direct outreach to drinking water well users with a meaningful approach to engage and involve community members and organizations: • Meet the community in suitable locations and at times when community members are available • Communicate in the preferred language of drinking water well users • Provide materials so community members can engage and understand technical information for a nontechnical audience. ... Briefing (can be done as webinar) on policy for all interested parties, with specific invitations to groups such as Self Help and Community Water Center and other known entities that work with impacted subbasin communities. Include translation.
records.notes: Webinar is an option, not a commitment; outcome in the following rows.

records.finding: Committee members agreed to the baseline outreach but wanted to defer the community briefing. One asked whether outreach could conflict with the State Board probation process and called the briefing a big lift.
records.agenda_item: Item 9: direction on domestic well mitigation policy outreach
records.evidence_text: Is there any concern with our… outreach efforts right now conflicting with our. have the probation… out of provision. Did we… there's situations where we… initiate conversations that could… called our probation to be reconsidered. Unreconsidered. only thought otherwise, we couldn't take it through it. Speaking from experience, yes. Um, the last one. Okay. I'll just… You can read between the lines there. I'd like to maybe hold off on the briefing. It seems like a pretty big lift. ... I feel comfortable, uh, that you would like me to go ahead and. implement the first four, which is completely in my existing scope.
records.notes: Speakers largely unlabelled; transcript garbled around 'probation'. The briefing was later scheduled (2026-05-19 row).

records.finding: The Coordination Committee's budget includes a $20,000 line for DAC outreach and coordination. It showed no spending, 100% remaining, in the February 2026 report.
records.quantitative_detail: Budget line DAC Outreach and Coordination: $20,000; spent $0; 100% remaining (budget-to-actual report in Feb 2026 packet)
records.agenda_item: Item 5c: budget to actual report
records.evidence_text: DAC Outreach and Coordination 20,000 $ -$ 20,000 $ 100%
records.notes: Budget table only; no meeting discussion of what the line will fund. Same unspent figure appears in the 2026-03-09 packet.

records.finding: The Delta-Mendota JPA board was told a domestic well policy workshop would be held 5 June 2026 with translations and a website recording, noticed through the subbasin newsletter. Earlier plans (March) had said late April, maximum 45 minutes.
records.quantitative_detail: Workshop date: 5 June 2026 (planned); 45 minutes maximum
records.agenda_item: Item: update on domestic well mitigation policy workshop
records.evidence_text: Chair just wanted to remind folks that this board previously directed us to hold a policy workshop in the springtime period Hallmark Group: to Taylor Blakslee: announce the well mitigation program. And so we're working with Lisa to schedule that domestic well policy workshop for the first week of June. So again we are intending to notice it in the newsletter that I understand you know is going out. And so we wanted to give folks enough time on the notice side. So we are looking to schedule that for June 5th. We'll have translations available, we'll have a recording on the website.
records.notes: No later meeting in scope reports attendance or whether the 5 June session took place; the 2026-06-03 committee meeting still describes it as upcoming.

records.finding: The Coordination Committee gave a go-ahead to a press release, a newsletter item and user-friendly flyers on the domestic well mitigation policy, posted on GSA and subbasin websites. A webinar or workshop for community groups stayed undecided pending cost review.
records.agenda_item: Item: outreach and engagement for well mitigation policy
records.evidence_text: the feedback from the coordination committee was yes, continue with a press release. Continue with information in the subbasin's newsletter. Yes, proceed with the informational flyers. Yes, proceed with GSA's posting of these user friendly flyers and the policy on their individual websites as well as the subbase and website which is part of that commitment that's in that well mitigation policy.
records.notes: Presenter relays the Coordination Committee's feedback; flyers' content not seen.

records.finding: The outreach consultant told the committee that flyers should be in English and Spanish and other languages as needed, and that all translation would be available to the subbasin at no cost through DWR's translation services.
records.quantitative_detail: Translation cost to GSAs: $0 (through DWR translation services)
records.agenda_item: Item 9: direction on domestic well mitigation policy outreach
records.evidence_text: you probably do need informational flyers in English and Spanish and other key audience languages as needed. ... All of the translation will be done and is available to you at no cost through DWR.
records.notes: Speaker is the facilitator (Lisa Beutler) per the surrounding turn-taking.

records.finding: The outreach team said the planned domestic well briefing would have translation services built in and that any NGOs involved would be asked to advertise it to their own audiences.
records.quantitative_detail: Briefing length: maximum 45 minutes; planned late April 2026
records.meeting_body: Joint meeting of Delta-Mendota Subbasin GSAs JPA Board and Coordination Committee
records.agenda_item: Item 22: update on facilitation, support services and outreach
records.evidence_text: Domestic. Well, outreach is being planned for late April looking to be maximum 45 minutes long. Translation services are being implemented as well. And then any NGOs that are involved will be asked to advertise that briefing to their own audiences on the newsletter.
records.notes: Presenter is the facilitation team (Holly Stanitsas).

records.finding: For its Delta-Mendota Subbasin item and the two small-pumper exclusion items that followed, the State Water Board provided live Spanish and Punjabi interpretation, simultaneous broadcast, translated presentation slides and headsets in the room and on Zoom.
records.quantitative_detail: Languages: Spanish, Punjabi; applies to items 3-5 of the 7 Apr 2026 agenda
records.meeting_body: State Water Board hearing (Delta-Mendota return to DWR; Tule and Tulare Lake minimal-impact exclusions)
records.agenda_item: Item 3 Delta-Mendota Subbasin; items 4-5
records.evidence_text: We're providing Spanish and Punjabi language interpretation services for this item, including the simultaneous broadcasting of this meeting in Spanish and Punjabi Spanish and Punjabi interpretation will also be provided for items four and five
records.notes: State Water Board practice at a hearing covering Delta-Mendota (item 3) and the Tule and Tulare Lake exclusion items (4-5); recorded under Delta-Mendota as the first item.

records.finding: As described to the Merced committees, the Delta-Mendota Subbasin's draft domestic well policy covers wells used for domestic supply as of November 19, 2024, commits to bottled water within 24 hours and reasonable efforts to provide tanked water within 72 hours, and is funded by a $300,000 common account shared equally; fewer than 40 wells were reported dry or applied for replacement in 10 years.
records.quantitative_detail: Common account $300,000; bottled water within 24 hours; tanked water within 72 hours (all reasonable efforts, case by case after site investigation); fewer than 40 wells reported dry or applied for replacement in 10 years over ~1,200 sq mi
records.speaker_role: mixed — Merced GSP slides presented by a Coordination Committee member
records.meeting_body: Merced GSP Coordination Committee and Stakeholder Advisory Committee (joint meeting)
records.agenda_item: 7. Domestic Well Mitigation Program Development Update
records.evidence_text: During the last 10 years, fewer than 40 wells across the nearly 1,200 square miles of the Subbasin have been reported dry or applied for replacement. ... Delivery of bottled water within 24 hours ... All reasonable efforts made to provide tanked water within seventy-two (72) hours. ... Delta-Mendota Subbasin Coordination Committee agree to equally fund a common account to a total of $300,000.
records.notes: Secondhand; the presenter said the policy was still draft pending state review of the revised GSP and a third of the account had been collected.

records.finding: SJREC's board was shown the domestic well mitigation policy it was asked to approve: up to $30,000 per dry existing well serving fewer than 14 connections, triggered by water levels below 2015. The party whose pumping caused the decline is expected to replenish a shared escrow.
records.quantitative_detail: Up to $30,000 per well; fewer than 14 connections; trigger = water levels below 2015 minimum threshold; escrow of $300,000 mentioned (speech garbled on who contributes)
records.agenda_item: Item 6: Domestic Well Mitigation Policy
records.evidence_text: This is for domestic water supply where there's fewer than 14 connections. ... we would be mitigating up to $30,000 per well if it met some criteria that would be vetted by the GSA ... the exchange contractors were a one seven partner now in sub basin, and so everybody's gonna put in one step, $300,000 into basically like an escrow account.
records.notes: Speaker is unlabelled (inferred to be the Authority's general manager from context); escrow sentence is garbled. Policy is the subbasin-wide one the board voted to approve in the same meeting.

records.finding: The revised Delta-Mendota Subbasin domestic well mitigation policy covers small water systems of up to 14 connections and sets reasonable-efforts targets of emergency water within 24 hours of a complete application and tanked water within 72 hours, in cooperation with Valley Water Collaborative and Self-Help Enterprises.
records.quantitative_detail: Emergency water: within 24 hours of complete application; tanked water: within 72 hours after site investigation; small water system: no more than 14 service connections
records.meeting_body: Madera County GSA Committee (staff report on Delta-Mendota Subbasin policy)
records.agenda_item: Item B: resolution adopting the revised Delta-Mendota Subbasin Domestic Well Mitigation Policy
records.evidence_text: The revised policy considers impacts to domestic wells, including small water systems defined as no more than 14 service connections. Additionally, updates have been made to the language regarding short-term emergency water supply response times. Now, reasonable efforts will be made to supply emergency water within 24 hours of submission of a complete application. Also, after additional site investigation, per GSA, reasonable efforts will be made to provide tanked water within 72 hours. This includes working with Valley Water Collaborative, Self-Help Enterprises, and other similar entities to assist with feasibility of providing water tanks.
records.notes: Staff report written by Madera County GSA about the subbasin-wide policy; the Coordination Committee (2025-09-08) said the revision followed State Water Board direction. Policy is a reasonable-efforts standard, not a guarantee. 23 GSAs were asked to adopt it.

records.finding: The subbasin keeps a joint domestic well mitigation fund, described as $300,000 held with $100,000 added annually. The June 2026 budget shows year two of three at $100,000.
records.quantitative_detail: $300,000 target account; $100,000 added annually (speaker unsure whether balance is $100,000 or $200,000); FY27 budget line 'Year 2 of 3': $100,000
records.agenda_item: Item 8: draft FY budget
records.evidence_text: the funding mitigation account, uh, which again, my understanding is, uh, there's gonna be $300,000 that would be, um, uh, held into an account with $100,000 added annually.
records.notes: Speaker uncertain about the current balance. The FY27 figure is from the 2026-06-08 JPA budget packet.

records.finding: Central Delta-Mendota GSA members reported that all had signed the Domestic Well Funding MOU except Merced County and Fresno County, whose boards were still to act. The GSA also adopted the subbasin policy that day.
records.agenda_item: Item 10: signatures on Domestic Well Funding MOU
records.evidence_text: Sam Cunningham/P&P provided the update that all members of the Central Delta-Mendota Region and GSA have signed the Domestic Well Funding MOU and acknowledged acceptance of the Fiscal Year 2026 SS-MOA Participation Percentage Letter, except for Merced County and Fresno County.
records.notes: Minutes text. Cost-share percentages are not shown.

records.finding: State Board staff said the Delta-Mendota GSAs revised and republished their domestic well mitigation policy in July 2025 after technical talks with Board staff, including the earlier lack of water-quality mitigation. Staff said the policy is now more comprehensive and recommended returning the subbasin to DWR.
records.quantitative_detail: Policy revised July 2025; 19 technical meetings between staff and GSAs
records.meeting_body: State Water Board hearing (Delta-Mendota return to DWR; Tule and Tulare Lake minimal-impact exclusions)
records.agenda_item: Item 3 Delta-Mendota Subbasin staff presentation
records.evidence_text: the GSA has revised and published the domestic well mitigation policy, incorporating the many technical conversations the GSA has had with State Water Board staff regarding mitigation issues, including the lack of water Quality mitigation.
records.notes: Terms (cap, eligibility) are not given in the passage.

records.finding: Under the policy, a mitigation request is paid from the JPA's collective fund and the GSA in whose area the well sits is expected to refund it, reportedly over two years. Staff urged GSAs to budget for well mitigation.
records.quantitative_detail: Repayment period: two years (speaker 'I believe so')
records.agenda_item: Item: FY27 GSA budgets
records.evidence_text: As it stands, the domestic well mitigation policy. We have, you know, a collective fund under the jpa. And so we just wanted to have that as a reminder that maybe at the GSA level budget. Consider budgeting for well mitigation. Because the way it works now is that if we were to get a request for mitigation, that would come out of our JPA fund. But the expectation is that it's refunded by the gsa that that mitigation is happening in. ... Over two years. Right. Is the repayment period for that? I believe so.
records.notes: Repayment period confirmed only tentatively by the speaker.

records.finding: Madera County GSA staff described an MOU between Valley Water Collaborative and the 23 Delta-Mendota GSAs on water-quality testing for domestic wells and replacement water, mainly to avoid duplicate effort and share data. The Collaborative tests for nitrate among other contaminants and delivers water to wells above the MCL.
records.quantitative_detail: 23 GSAs party to the MOU; Madera County GSA described as the last to sign
records.agenda_item: Item 5: MOU with Valley Water Collaborative on domestic well testing and replacement water
records.evidence_text: Valley Water Collaborative provides nitrate testing on… Among other contaminant testing for domestic wells. Madera County: They also provide water deliveries for those domestic wells that. Exceed the state's maximum contaminant level. ... The main goal of this MOU is to avoid duplication efforts and to share data.
records.notes: Staff and a director both speak; the presentation is by staff. Also relevant to COM-3.3.2b.

records.finding: EKI told the Coordination Committee that many water-quality monitoring wells still lack sustainable management criteria because data are missing, especially for 1,2,3-TCP, gross alpha, chromium 6 and arsenic. Preliminary criteria could be set for some wells after one full year of sampling.
records.quantitative_detail: One full year of sampling needed per well before preliminary criteria; seasonal-high sampling March to May 2026
records.meeting_body: Joint meeting of Delta-Mendota Subbasin GSAs JPA Board and Coordination Committee
records.agenda_item: Item 20: GSP implementation updates (water quality SMC development)
records.evidence_text: As you know when we developed the GSP a lot of the water quality RMW do not have SMC established due to lack of data or water quality measurements especially for certain constituents of concern like 1 2, 32 CP, Gross Alpha, Chrom 6 and Arsenic. And since 2024 some well have collected data and also like in 2025. So with the data collected so far we are able to establish preliminary SMC for some of those wells after one full year of sampling.
records.notes: Presenter identified as EKI by surrounding labels; the wells are SGMA representative monitoring wells, not domestic wells.

records.finding: State Board staff summarised the Delta-Mendota GSAs' water-quality changes: a larger monitoring network, semi-annual sampling, and a water quality mitigation policy for domestic users that uses the Valley Water Collaborative for well testing and replacement water under CV-SALTS.
records.quantitative_detail: Water-quality representative network expanded from 70 to 90 sites; semi-annual sampling; TDS above secondary MCL of 1,000 mg/L across the subbasin (as presented)
records.meeting_body: State Water Board hearing (Delta-Mendota return to DWR; Tule and Tulare Lake minimal-impact exclusions)
records.agenda_item: Item 3 Delta-Mendota Subbasin staff presentation
records.evidence_text: the GSAs expanded the representative monitoring network from 70 sites to 90, and increased the monitoring frequency to semi annual sampling for monitoring
records.notes: Staff summary of GSA revisions, not GSA speech. Constituent list beyond TDS and nitrate not stated in this passage.

records.finding: Subbasin staff reported six TDS and nitrate exceedances across the basin but said data-quality problems and incomplete reporting in the data management system mean these may not be the only ones.
records.quantitative_detail: Six TDS and nitrate exceedances (preliminary review, Q2 2026 reporting cycle)
records.agenda_item: Report items: pumping reduction plan exceedance reporting
records.evidence_text: our preliminary review showed that there were six exceedances of TDS and NITRATE across the basin. But again due to some quality issues, data quality issues in the DMS or incomplete reporting, we can't say that these are the only exceedances with confidence.
records.notes: Speaker unlabelled (consultant team inferred). Which quarter the six exceedances belong to was not confirmed.

records.finding: The policy's required commitments include exceedance notifications to domestic well owners that explain the policy and how to file a mitigation claim. GSA-level outreach and postcards are optional.
records.agenda_item: Item 9: direction on domestic well mitigation policy outreach
records.evidence_text: Exceedance Notifications to domestic well owners to include information on policy and how to file a mitigation claim
records.notes: Packet memo from the plan manager and facilitator.

records.finding: EKI described the notice step for a confirmed nitrate exceedance above the MCL: notify domestic well users within roughly a 2 to 3 mile radius, with the speaker believing the plan says 3 miles. A flowchart was provided to GSAs.
records.quantitative_detail: Notification radius: 2 to 3 miles (speaker 'believes' 3 miles per the plan)
records.agenda_item: Item: PRP and well mitigation exceedance flowchart
records.evidence_text: a notification to domestic well Coordination Committee (SLDMWA Board Room): users within Anona Dutton (EKI): a 2 to Coordination Committee (SLDMWA Board Room): 3 Anona Dutton (EKI): mile radius ... I Anona Dutton (EKI): believe it's 3 mile radius
records.notes: Transcript alternates two speaker labels mid-sentence; radius not confirmed against the policy text. A procedural step done by GSAs by hand.

records.finding: SJREC's board was told water-quality mitigation is owed only if the GSAs' water-level decline below 2015 thresholds, or a new project, mobilizes certain constituents (chromium 6 and 1,2,3-TCP among them); nitrate and TDS are excluded from the level-based condition. The cap is $2,500 per well.
records.quantitative_detail: Mitigation up to $2,500 per well for water quality; water-level trigger = 2015 minimum thresholds
records.agenda_item: Item 6: Domestic Well Mitigation Policy
records.evidence_text: so long as we maintain water level above 2015, water quality problems, we didn't cause it. ... Nitrates and TDs would be excluded from from that mitigation ... you would be on the hook for mitigating up to $2,500 per well, and it would be at the discretion of how they want to mitigate that.
records.notes: Garbled transcription of constituent names ('Ryo', 'Chrome six', '123, TCP'); the speaker is inferred. See subbasin policy text in the Madera County GSA 2025-10-07 packet.

records.finding: The subbasin policy ties domestic-well water-quality mitigation to GSA actions: it applies if a project or management action, or a water-level fall below the 2015 minimum thresholds, pushes any of six constituents past its minimum threshold. Water-quality data thus feeds a mitigation trigger.
records.quantitative_detail: Six constituents of concern: TDS, nitrate, gross alpha, chromium VI, arsenic, 1,2,3-TCP; water-level trigger = 2015 minimum thresholds
records.meeting_body: Madera County GSA Committee (staff report on Delta-Mendota Subbasin policy)
records.agenda_item: Item B: resolution adopting the revised Delta-Mendota Subbasin Domestic Well Mitigation Policy
records.evidence_text: Domestic well mitigation would be required for water quality if any Project or Management Action (P/MA) by the GSA caused water quality degradation beyond the Minimum Thresholds (MTs) for the 6 constituents of concern (Total Dissolved Solids (TDS), Nitrate, Gross Alpha, Chromium VI, Arsenic, and 1,2,3-Trichloropropane (TCP)). Similarly, water quality would need to be addressed for a domestic well if groundwater levels decline below 2015 MTs and cause water quality degradation beyond water quality MTs for the 6 constituents of concern.
records.notes: Also answers COM-3.3.2a (six constituents). Staff report, not the policy text itself.

records.finding: In Q3 2026 the Northern region recorded repeat nitrate, new TDS and chromium 6 exceedances. EKI checked each for pumping reduction plan triggers and found none, mainly because there were too few samples to correlate water quality with water levels.
records.quantitative_detail: Q3 2026: 2 repeat nitrate exceedances, 1 new TDS exceedance, 2 chromium 6 exceedances; 0 PRP triggers
records.agenda_item: Item 13: PRP implementation update
records.evidence_text: In Q3 there were two repeat nitrate nitrate exceedances, one new TDS exceedance and two Chrome 6 exceedances. So given that we had these MT exceedances, we did an initial investigation on these wells and determined there were no PRP triggers for any of those wells that exceeded. In most cases it was because there weren't enough samples yet to establish a correlation between water levels and water quality.
records.notes: Shows water quality being screened against a pumping-reduction (accounting) trigger. Earlier watch-list handling in the same body on 2026-06-03 and 2026-07-01.

records.section: 3.3.3 Domestic Wells and Community Water System Consolidation
records.finding: Madera County GSA staff say there are no domestic wells on the lands covered by its Delta-Mendota area and no funding source for mitigation there. The basis for the no-wells statement (inventory, county records) is not given.
records.agenda_item: Item 5: MOU with Valley Water Collaborative
records.evidence_text: It is important to note that currently there are no domestic wells located on the lands covered by Madera County GSA Delta Mendota. Madera County: And no funding source for avail… No funding sources available for will mitigation through the county GSA Delta Mendota.
records.notes: A grower on 2025-10-07 said water there is about 15 feet deep and asked whether any wells needed redrilling; no data source was cited by staff.

records.finding: EKI gave the State Water Board an interactive map of water fill station locations ahead of its July 2025 meeting. The minutes do not say who uses the stations or what data the map contains.
records.quantitative_detail: State Water Board meeting date: 22 July 2025
records.agenda_item: Item 11a: program management report
records.evidence_text: EKI provided water fill stations location interactive map to the SWCRB ahead of the July 22, 2025 meeting.
records.notes: One line in the minutes; purpose of the stations (e.g. for households with dry wells) is not stated.

records.finding: The subbasin website is being rebuilt with a specific page for domestic well mitigation, covering the water-level program and the Valley Water Collaborative water-quality MOU. The policy requires an electronic claim form, which still has to be built.
records.meeting_body: Joint meeting of Delta-Mendota Subbasin GSAs JPA Board and Coordination Committee
records.agenda_item: Item: website update
records.evidence_text: there is a specific page that we had anticipated for the domestic well mitigation and there was two parts of that. There was the groundwater level mitigation program and then the MOA with the Valley Water Collaborative for the water quality piece. So having both of those and the well mitigation plan even requires us to have a form they can submit electronically. So that's something that we still need to develop.
records.notes: Speaker is the plan manager (Taylor Blakslee inferred). The 2026-02-04 board also reviewed the website plan.

records.finding: A LandWatch letter citing ERA's March 2026 analysis puts Eastside temporary fallowing for a 10% pumping cut at $1,500-1,800/AF and permanent fallowing at $670-760/AF. Staff separately named the Eastside as an area for MLRP repurposing concepts (2026-10-07).
records.quantitative_detail: Temporary fallowing $1,500-$1,800 per AF; 10% of Eastside pumping = 7,773 AF; total $11,659,500-$13,991,400 (letter's calculation); permanent fallowing $670-$760 per AF (ERA Table 18 as cited). Time basis not stated.
records.speaker_role: NGO/advocate — LandWatch Monterey County (letter citing ERA Economics)
records.agenda_item: 3.2 Integrated Implementation Strategy PMA Final Portfolios (letter dated 2026-07-11 in packet)
records.evidence_text: For the Eastside, the direct cost of temporary land fallowing to achieve a 10% reduction in pumping is $1,500 to $1,800 per AF. ... the direct cost of permanent land fallowing in the Eastside, which ERA determined to be from $670 to $760 per AF.
records.notes: Secondary citation by an advocate; check against ERA's Demand Management Economic Impact Analysis (March 2026).

records.finding: In the Eastside the consultant analysed nitrate, gross alpha and 1,2,3-TCP. The only significant result was a weak inverse correlation between nitrate and extraction in exact well pairs, driven by Quail Creek wells over coarse sediments, which staff attribute to local geology rather than a subbasin-wide pumping effect.
records.quantitative_detail: Groundwater-level trend period 1995-2024
records.meeting_body: SVBGSA 180/400-Ft Aquifer and Eastside Subbasin Committees (joint session)
records.agenda_item: 4.2 Recommended Corrective Action - Water Quality
records.evidence_text: For E that was nitrate, gross alpha radioactivity and 1, 2, 3 TCP. ... What we see in the results is that we actually have an inverse relationship. So those smaller pumpers have higher concentrations or increasing concentrations of nitrates. ... the wells that have the highest concentrations there in that dot are all within that Quail Creek area.
records.notes: 'For E' is the transcript's rendering of 'For Eastside'; the correlation disappeared when nearby wells were paired.

records.finding: Madera County GSA staff told the committee that its 2026 Summary of Rules booklet includes a progress update on the Lavinia Pilot Project, which they describe as one of its Multi Benefit Land Repurposing projects, plus a Land Repurposing page on programme status. No grantee, grant amount or day-to-day administrator was named in the meeting.
records.agenda_item: 4d. Informational item: 2026 Summary of Rules booklet publication and outreach
records.evidence_text: We provided a update on one of the Multi Benefit Land Repurposing Program which is Lavinia Pilot Project ... The Land Repurposing page provides an overview of the multi benefit land repurposing program and the current status with implementation
records.notes: Speaker is the senior administrative analyst introducing the booklet. The pilot project is not described further in the transcript.

records.finding: Madera County GSA staff said 'fallow' means different things to different people, that field visits have been done and that the GSA still needs to decide what it means by fallow; a matrix of what is fallowed could be developed but is not in the annual-report contract.
records.agenda_item: Informational item: Davids Engineering annual report agreement
records.evidence_text: Looking ahead that we can develop is more of a matrix on exactly what is followed. I will say this follow means different things to different people and we have done a fair amount of field visits and we need to decide what we mean by fallow
records.notes: Speaker is the Director of Water and Natural Resources answering a supervisor; the transcript renders fallow as followed.

records.finding: Hydrosat's proposal to Madera County GSA says it will update land use maps yearly using a summer fallow analysis that changes ETAW for fields that cross between fallow and crops, provide parcel and farm-unit water budgets updated monthly, and check fallow fields mid-season to flag fields for on-ground verification.
records.agenda_item: Item 4a: Hydrosat measurement data presentation (proposal in packet)
records.evidence_text: Hydrosat's approach will be to update these maps on annual basis based on 1) fallow analysis that will be done during summer to detect fallowed land that has moved into cropping systems and cropped areas that have turned into fallow. This will affect the ETAW of these fields; ... Customized portal tables for parcel water budgets and farm unit budgets updated monthly ... Mid-season check of fallow fields and assisting in defining the fields that needs on- ground verification
records.notes: Vendor proposal text in the committee packet, not GSA policy; the committee later chose Hydrosat as the single satellite provider.

records.finding: Madera County GSA's allocation resolution treats land that was irrigated since 2015 but is now fallowed or idle as irrigated land for allocation purposes, allocates transitional water only to land irrigated at adoption, and limits allocations to use within the parcel or farm unit. The text does not say an allocation is forfeited when land is fallowed.
records.quantitative_detail: Land irrigated as of June 8, 2021, or last irrigated on or after January 1, 2015, counts as irrigated land for allocation
records.agenda_item: Packet: draft resolutions on farm unit annual changes and 2026-2040 allocation tables
records.evidence_text: WHEREAS, irrigated land includes agricultural lands that are currently irrigated as of June 8, 2021, or were last irrigated as recently as January 1, 2015, but now may otherwise be non-irrigated (e.g. fallowed or idle). ... Groundwater allocations shall be limited to use within the parcel or within the designated farm unit. ... Transitional water will only be allocated to lands that are considered irrigated lands as of the date of the adoption of this Resolution.
records.notes: Resolution recitals in the agenda packet; the County GSA resolutions apply to the Madera, Chowchilla and Delta-Mendota subbasins. Forfeiture is not mentioned either way, so this is an inference from silence.

records.finding: A county supervisor on the committee said some Madera County GSA policies make it more sensible for growers to plant non-irrigated acres than to retire water, and that the GSA needs a way to help growers retire water while keeping a disincentive against overuse.
records.agenda_item: 4e. Informational item: review of fallow fields data
records.evidence_text: some instances, it makes more sense to plant not non irrigated acres instead of, you know, retiring that water. So we have to figure out a way that we can help folks retire water when it makes sense for them but also make sure that there's, you know, a disincentive in place that actually encourage people not to overuse
records.notes: Speaker is unlabelled but is the committee supervisor asked for comments immediately before. The remark is a general policy comment; the transcript does not explain how allocations are treated when water is retired.

records.finding: In an illustrative scenario, Madera County GSA staff showed that a recently fallowed 100-acre parcel keeps its allocation (200 AF at 2 AF per acre for 2027) and can contribute it to a combined farm unit with an irrigated neighbour, giving 600 AF for the pooled unit. Scenario numbers are examples.
records.quantitative_detail: Illustrative: 2 AF per acre allocation in 2027 (Madera Subbasin); fallowed 100 acres = 200 AF; irrigated 200 acres = 400 AF; combined farm unit = 600 AF ETAW
records.agenda_item: Informational item: how growers use farm units
records.evidence_text: Farm A is 100 acres, it's very recently fallowed, so theoretically has no water use, no evapotranspiration of applied water or etaw, it has no carryover. And I'm just going to kind of make a caveat. It says no recharge potential. And really what that means is it's not near a water source. So if water became legally available, it has no ability to take it because it's just not near water. So if it's 100 acres and the allocation is 2 acre feet per acre, that allocation is 200 acre feet in 2027. ... So you can see if farm A and farm B joined together in a farm unit, provided us with a lease agreement or any other agreement, it would be 300 acres total. 200 acres would be irrigated and the allocation would be 600 acre feet of evapotranspiration of applied water.
records.notes: The meeting was recorded twice (also 46800d5b-ae1a-4042-b1e8-2d1e0c8d97a6, same date). Numbers are hypothetical scenarios built by staff, not actual accounts. Speaker is the Director of Water and Natural Resources presenting.

records.finding: Madera County GSA staff reported that, among allocating agencies in their survey, theirs is the only one with no expiry on carryover and the only one with multiple satellite measurement methods. Public commenters at the same meeting opposed adding expiry.
records.agenda_item: Informational item: demand management policy options
records.evidence_text: We are the only agency that doesn't have a carryover policy where there's an expiration on the carryover. And we're also the only agency with multiple satellite measurement methods.
records.notes: Speaker is the Director of Water and Natural Resources presenting policy options. The survey comparison table is in the 2025-10-07 packet (Madera: no expiration, no decay). Applies to the County GSA allocations in the Madera Subbasin; a Chowchilla version is not separate. Staff said the survey was shared at the previous committee meeting. Basin-wide rule; not specific to repurposed land.

records.finding: A Madera Subbasin commenter proposed using penalty revenue to pay growers for unused water credits and letting growers sell credits to one another, arguing that without a market growers who build up credits will plant to use them. This is a public proposal, not a GSA policy.
records.agenda_item: Public comment (carryover credits)
records.evidence_text: it would be a great approach to pay growers for those water credits with the penalty dollars that are coming in. ... we need to begin considering whether growers can sell their water credits to one another. ... if we start to limit water credits, there's no market for water credits. There's no way to do anything with them. And it's going to cause growers to start planting.
records.notes: Commenter is a Madera Subbasin grower speaking in public comment; the point was repeated on 2026-04-07 with a request for a combined meeting on penalties, penalty revenue and carryover credits. Staff made no commitment. Basin-wide rule; not specific to repurposed land.

records.finding: Madera County GSA staff described farm units, formed under a lease or other written agreement of one year, five years or perpetuity, as the way growers share allocation and carryover across parcels; in the example, fallowed parcels contribute carryover to a larger irrigated farm. Credit sales are not the stated mechanism.
records.quantitative_detail: Illustrative: combined farm unit of A, B and C = 3,300 AF
records.agenda_item: Informational item: how growers use farm units
records.evidence_text: And the agreement with the growers could be just for a year, it could be for five years, tied to a GSP cycle, maybe, or it could be in perpetuity. ... Farm C is bringing carryover from not using the water. And they're both contributing in terms of the allocation to farm B, the larger farm.
records.notes: Scenario numbers are hypothetical. The 2025-09-02 and 2025-10-07 committee items adopt the farm-unit carryover and penalty split policy (default volumetric apportionment unless an agreement says otherwise). Geographic limits: farm unit zones, with a request to link north and south zones raised and deferred.

records.finding: Madera County GSA staff said they ran a water-market pilot under a Bureau of Reclamation grant in 2019-2020, found tracking the trades took a fair amount of work, and called market trading an ongoing discussion.
records.quantitative_detail: Water-market pilot 2019-2020 (Bureau of Reclamation grant); no volumes given
records.agenda_item: Informational item: how growers use farm units
records.evidence_text: We did do a pilot project with water markets through a Bureau of reclamation grant in 2019. 2020. And it was interesting. It was a fair amount of work to track the trades. So I know the intention is always something is simple and clear and straightforward, but it ended up being a fair amount more complicated. Okay. And then I don't think it's a dead discussion. I think it's an ongoing discussion on how that could or should look
records.notes: Speaker is the Director of Water and Natural Resources answering a supervisor. On 2026-02-03 a commenter asked whether a market for voluntarily trading allocations is planned; the chair said it had been discussed before. A grower commenter asked for a simple credit transfer form instead of redrawing farm units; staff offered to follow up. Basin-wide rule; not specific to repurposed land.

records.finding: Staff analysed fallowing through irrigated acreage for 2016-2024 and found no substantial decrease in irrigated acres in the Madera Subbasin County GSA area, and compared ETAW (water use) with the allocation. No direct count of fallowed acres or fallowing savings was described.
records.quantitative_detail: Irrigated acreage 2016-2024, annual series; no substantial decrease (no acreage figure given in the speech)
records.agenda_item: 4e. Informational item: review of fallow fields data
records.evidence_text: We have found that it's easier to look at irrigated acres than fallowed fields and that we have a good source for irrigated acres. ... So in the Madera Subbasin County GSA we do not see a substantial decrease in irrigated acres over time.
records.notes: Speaker is the Director of Water and Natural Resources per the item introduction. The chart shows ETAW against allocation but the transcript gives no ETAW figures from staff.

records.finding: Madera County GSA staff floated a formal fallow-fields programme in which a grower notifies the GSA and staff zero out that field's ETAW (the satellite measurement), while still measuring it in the background. It is an idea for development, not an adopted rule.
records.agenda_item: Informational item: look back and look ahead for 2026
records.evidence_text: Another idea we had is a more formal fallow fields program. We do let people fallow fields and people do this all the time as part of standard farming practices. A fallow field program could have people notify us and then we could zero out their ET aw, essentially zeroing out the satellite measurement although we can measure it in the background so there's the potential for a program there.
records.notes: Speaker is the Director of Water and Natural Resources giving the annual look-ahead. The 2026-05-05 committee update says no fallow fields programme exists yet.

records.finding: In Madera County GSA's ledger, savings from fallowing appear only as unused allocation: in staff's example a parcel fallowed a couple of years earlier holds 400 AF of carryover that can be pooled into a farm unit. No separate fallowing or land-repurposing credit was described.
records.quantitative_detail: Illustrative: 400 AF carryover on a 100-acre parcel fallowed a couple of years earlier
records.agenda_item: Informational item: how growers use farm units
records.evidence_text: farm C, 100 acres. It is similar to the one a couple scenarios ago where it has been fallowed. This, however, fallowed a couple of years ago. So it has carryover of 400 acre feet. ... Farm C is bringing carryover from not using the water.
records.notes: Scenario is hypothetical. The inference that there is no separate fallow credit is from the examples given, not an explicit staff statement.

records.section: 2.5 Data Source and ET Product Choice
records.finding: Land IQ's proposal in the Madera County GSA packet describes monthly field-by-field remotely sensed ET delivered within 30 days of month end, calibrated against about 100 climatic ground-truthing stations that are also used for validation datasets. No local field validation in Madera is described.
records.quantitative_detail: About 100 climatic ground-truthing stations; monthly delivery within 30 days; coverage about 3.5 million acres (all clients)
records.agenda_item: Item 4b: Land IQ measurement data presentation (proposal in packet)
records.evidence_text: A monthly remotely sensed ET field-by-field measurement is performed and delivered to the districts within 30 days following the end of the previous month. ... The ground truthing stations are also used for validation datasets.
records.notes: Vendor proposal text in the committee packet. The validation stations are climatic stations, not Madera field measurements. Basin-wide rule; not specific to repurposed land.

records.section: 2.5 Data Source and ET Product Choice
records.finding: Staff reported that in 2023 half of Madera County GSA farm units defaulted to Land IQ (no response or incomplete meter data), against 28% choosing IrriWatch and 15% meters, and priced the satellite methods with extra consultant QA/QC. Staff said complaints about satellite measurement had dropped.
records.quantitative_detail: 2023 farm units by method: 28% IrriWatch, 7% Land IQ, 15% meters, 50% defaulted to Land IQ; 2023 cost $176,000 Hydrosat, about $100,000 Land IQ (fiscal basis not stated)
records.agenda_item: Informational item: measurement methods and costs
records.evidence_text: In 2023, the original measurement method Organized by farm units shows that 28% chose Earwatch, and 7% chose Land IQ, and there was 15% on Meters. And then 50% defaulted to Land IQ. ... hydrostat, for example, in 2023 was $176,000. records.section: 2.5 Data Source and ET Product Choice
records.finding: Madera County GSA staff recommended a three-year Hydrosat (formerly IrriWatch) contract as the single satellite ET provider because 52% of questionnaire respondents preferred it and most opposed funding two methods. records.finding: A Madera Ag Water Association representative disputed the grower questionnaire as a basis for choosing Hydrosat, saying it covered 35,000 of 87,000 enrolled acres and that actual use is roughly 37% Land IQ and 36% IrriWatch. He said members wanted continued use of Land IQ.

records.finding: The 2022 GSP project fee that was meant to fund land repurposing, recharge, water purchases and domestic well mitigation was enjoined by a court, leaving projects unbuilt and unfunded. The County GSAs in those subbasins refunded the fees that were paid in 2022 prior to the Court’s order and were enjoined from collecting fees in 2023 and 2024, leaving projects unbuilt and unfunded. ... A limited rate for domestic well mitigation only • $67/acre in a farm unit for three years; then $43/acre thereafter

records.section: 3.1.4 Domestic Well Protection as an Equity Outcome
records.finding: Applicants are screened out if their well went dry before 1 January 2026, unless they are on Self-Help's interim assistance list. No analysis of impacts by community (DAC versus other) was presented.

records.notes: On 2025-11-12 Madera Ag Water Association asked for a 2020 eligibility date; the rule adopted differs. Renters are not covered (landowners only) per the 2025-11-12 rules.

records.finding: To design its program Madera County GSA met agencies, nonprofits and community groups: Chowchilla WD's program team, two nitrate management zones, Self-Help Enterprises, Madera Ag Water Association, Madera Ranchos residents and Fairmead and Friends. Staff reported each group's feedback to the committee.
records.quantitative_detail: Six or more groups consulted; attendance not given
records.agenda_item: Item C: resolution to adopt rules for domestic well mitigation in the Madera Subbasin
records.evidence_text: When drafting the rules and the application process, our team engage with local agencies, nonprofits and community groups to identify what works best. ... We next met with two groups, the first one being committed Madera Ranchers, folks from Madera Ranchers and these are the groups that will be using the program, the folks at Mandera Ranchos. They had no objections to the 35,000 funding cap, which was viewed as reasonable support. They did ask for clear rules for multiple property wells and education for local well drillers so they can help guide homeowners through the program and supportive programs. They also suggested adding a disclaimer that no property liens will result from assistance and including well deepening options as an eligible criteria, not just full replacements. There were concerns about fairness and preventing misuse of funds, along with requests for clear financial reporting, including how money is spent and participation numbers. And finally, they suggested using simple slogans instead of domestic well mitigation, which can sound like legal jargon. And lastly, we visited with the Fairmead and Friends community group whose focus appeared to be more on accessibility and transparency.
records.notes: Focus groups with Madera Ranchos and Fairmead are described by staff and by a Fairmead speaker as held the month before (about October 2025).

Each property may receive well mitigation once, which will be recorded on the property deed to prevent duplicate funding.

records.finding: Madera County GSA's mitigation process: eligibility screening, a well inspection report by GSA-hired well consultants, denial letters with next steps where the cause is not groundwater decline, review of well-drilling quotes, and an approved amount fixed in the landowner agreement. Replacement drilling is the main method.
records.quantitative_detail: Cap $35,000 per well
records.agenda_item: Item 4D: amend the Domestic Well Mitigation Program
records.evidence_text: If all program requirements are met, our well consultants who specialize in in well site investigations, well design and water quality and our staff with geologists and hydrogeologists will conduct an inspection to determine the cause of the well failure. They will prepare a well inspection report which is reviewed by both GSA staff and the program administrator. If the well is fell due to reasons other than declining groundwater levels or subsidence, the report will document that and a denial letter will be sent to the property owner explaining the reason and where possible, providing guidance on next steps. This can include maintenance and recommendations and or referrals to other programs. Finally, if the property owner and well meet all eligibility criteria, GSA staff and the program administrator review multiple well drilling quotes and approve only the reasonable costs associated with the selected quote.
records.notes: The 2026-02-03 meeting adds a three-bid rule (two from a prequalified list) and GSA advances of funds to the landowner; speed of delivery was not reported.

records.finding: PV Water staff told the board the ISW indicator has only aspirational targets (no minimum threshold) because surface water is described as losing to groundwater, so pumping is not expected to worsen conditions. records.agenda_item: 10A. Receive Summary of SGMA Annual Report, Water Year 2025
records.evidence_text: Last one, second to last one is interconnected surface waters. This is indicator that we only established aspirational targets for. The reason for that is that surface water in the basin and groundwater largely have a disconnected relationship where it's surface water losing water to groundwater. Groundwater is not typically feeding surface water resources in the basin. If it was and if we were pumping more intensely, it could decline and have an effect on it. But because there's already that separated relationship, there's not really any expectation that it would worsen. And so we set those aspirational targets for the five represented monitoring points we have. And we were able to achieve five out of five for the interim milestones. But we did not achieve any of their measurable objectives in the prior year for 2025.

records.finding: In the PV Water rate study, staff re-estimated annual water use per rural residential connection (from district deliveries divided by connections) and cut the billing assumption from 0.5 to 0.4 AF, lowering the typical household augmentation bill about 20% even as the per-AF charge rises. This is a distributive fee-equity adjustment for domestic users.
records.quantitative_detail: Assumed use per rural residential connection: 0.66 AF/yr (before 2015), about 0.52 rounded to 0.5 (2015 study), about 0.39 rounded to 0.4 AF/yr (2026 study); per-AF charge +4.6%/yr average over five years; household bill about $163 now, $132 next year, back to $164 in year five
records.meeting_body: Pajaro Valley Water Management Agency GSA Board
records.agenda_item: Rate study update
records.evidence_text: So we did another analysis and back in 2000, so before 2015, every rural residential customer was billed for an estimated usage of 0.66 acre feet. 2015, we analyzed the data from Central Water District, San Andreas Mutual and Romas and we know total deliveries, total connections, do the math. And it was about 0.5, 0.52. I think we rounded down and I ran through that same exercise again, and now the number looks to be more like 0.39. So we rounded to 0.4. So what that does is, you can see we put it on here in two rows because it's. It was a little confusing. Rural residential charge by acre foot is actually going up 4.6% per year on average over five years. But because they're now going to be billed at 4/10 of an acre foot instead of 5/10 of an acre foot, their rate is going down by about 20%. So right now they pay 163 acre, 3. $163 per acre household connected to the well. Next year it would drop to 132 and then eventually build back up to $164 in five years from now
records.notes: Speaker is staff/manager reporting; the June 18 presentation says the method divides deliveries from Central Water District, Aromas Water District and San Andreas Water Mutual by connections, same as 2015, and gives 2021-2025 data.
